expected_symptom: A DXIL module that uses SV_ViewID but omits, zeroes or falsifies dx.viewIdState should be rejected by DXIL validation; the issue says it is accepted.
godbolt_skip: The symptom is not visible in a Compiler Explorer pane. It lives in dxv/IDxcValidator run over a DXIL module that DXC did not produce -- the modules are hand-edited (dx.viewIdState deleted, zeroed, or falsified), and CE compiles HLSL with dxc and shows the resulting DXIL. It has no way to feed a doctored module back into the validator, and repro.hlsl on its own compiles cleanly on every DXC (that is the control, variant-control-dxc-pipeline). A CE link would show a clean compile and be read as no-repro.
summary: Accurate and unaddressed. createComputeViewIdStatePass() is called only from the compile pipeline (PassManagerBuilder.cpp:391,709) and the linker (DxilLinker.cpp:1293), never from lib/DxilValidation/, so validation has no recomputed state to compare against. Measured with dxv over hand-edited modules from a vs_6_1 shader reading SV_ViewID: deleting dx.viewIdState, zeroing its dependency words, and replacing them with a deliberately false mapping all report 'Validation succeeded.' on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all four releases that ship dxv (v1.8.2505 through v1.9.2607), while an out-of-range storeOutput sig id and a vs_6_0 downgrade are rejected everywhere - so the validator does read the dx.op.viewID call, it just never checks it against the state. PR #6859 (2024) added PSVContentVerifier::VerifyViewIDDependence, which compares the PSV0 part with DM.GetSerializedViewIdState() (two copies of the same producer-supplied metadata) and returns early when the module state is empty and PSV is all zero, so it does not close the gap. Enhancement, not a bug: nothing DXC emits is wrong and nothing regressed; the exposure is to third-party DXIL producers and to drivers that trust the state.
title: DXIL validation should run ComputeViewIdState pass
